text:
“How the sight of other people’s life and happiness makes those wish to live who, the day before, in the solitude of their souls and in the shadows of their sickrooms, wished to die quickly!”

<tb>

“10 January:

“This hope of health was only a dream. Here I am back in my bed, my body covered with plasters that burn me. Go, then, and offer this body for which people once paid so dearly, and see what they will give you for it today!

“We must have done a great deal of evil before we were born, or else be destined to enjoy very great happiness after our death, for God to allow this life to contain all the torments of expiation and all the sufferings of trial.”

<tb>

“12 January:

“I am still suffering.

“The Comte de N... sent me money yesterday; I did not accept it. I want nothing from that man. It is because of him that you are not here beside me.

“Oh, our beautiful days at Bougival! Where are you?

“If I leave this room alive, it will be to make a pilgrimage to the house where we lived together; but I shall leave it only when I am dead.

“Who knows whether I shall write to you tomorrow?”

<tb>

“25 January:

“For eleven nights now I have not slept; I have been suffocating and believing at every moment that I am about to die. The doctor ordered that I not be allowed to touch a pen. Julie Duprat, who watches over me, is still allowing me to write you these few lines. Will you not come back, then, before I die? Is it over between us forever, then? It seems to me that, if you came, I would recover. What would be the use of recovering?”

<tb>

“28 January:

“This morning I was awakened by a great commotion. Julie, who was sleeping in my room, rushed into the dining room. I heard men’s voices against which hers struggled in vain. She came back in tears.

“They had come to seize my property. I told her to let them carry out what they call justice. The bailiff entered my room with his hat on his head. He opened the drawers, recorded everything he saw, and did not appear to notice that there was a dying woman in the bed which, fortunately, the charity of the law allows me to keep.

“As he was leaving, he consented to tell me that I could lodge an objection within nine days, but he left a custodian behind! What is to become of me, my God! This scene has made me even more ill. Prudence wanted to ask your father’s friend for money; I opposed it.

“I received your letter this morning. I needed it. Will my reply reach you in time? Will you see me again? This has been a happy day, making me forget all those I have spent during the past six weeks. It seems to me that I am better, despite the feeling of sadness under whose influence I replied to you.

“After all, one should not always be unhappy.

“When I think that it may happen that I do not die, that you come back, that I see the spring again, that you still love me, and that we begin our life of last year again!

“What a madwoman I am! I can scarcely hold the pen with which I am writing you this senseless dream of my heart.

“Whatever happens, I loved you dearly, Armand, and I would have died long ago if I did not have, to sustain me, the memory of that love and a vague hope of seeing you beside me once more.”

<tb>

“4 February:

“The Comte de G... has returned. His mistress betrayed him. He is very sad; he loved her very much. He came to tell me all about it. The poor fellow is in rather bad financial circumstances, which did not prevent him from paying my bailiff and dismissing the custodian.

“I spoke to him about you, and he promised to speak to you about me. How completely I forgot at such moments that I had been his mistress, and how he tried to make me forget it too! He has a good heart.

“The duke sent to inquire after me yesterday, and he came this morning. I do not know what can still be keeping that old man alive. He remained beside me for three hours and did not say twenty words to me. Two large tears fell from his eyes when he saw me so pale. The memory of his daughter’s death was no doubt making him weep. He must have seen her die twice. His back is bent, his head inclines toward the ground, his lip droops, his gaze is lifeless. Age and sorrow weigh with their double burden upon his exhausted body. He did not reproach me. One might even have said that he secretly delighted in the devastation the illness had wrought in me. He seemed proud to be standing when I, still young, was crushed by suffering.

“The bad weather has returned. No one comes to see me. Julie watches beside me as much as she can. Prudence, to whom I can no longer give as much money as I once did, is beginning to make business affairs a pretext for staying away.

“Now that I am close to death, despite what the doctors tell me—for I have several of them, which proves that the illness is worsening—I almost regret having listened to your father. If I had known that I would take only one year from your future, I would not have resisted the desire to spend that year with you, and at least I would be dying while holding a friend’s hand. It is true that if we had lived together this year, I would not have died so soon.

“May God’s will be done!”

<tb>

“5 February:

“Oh! Come, come, Armand; I am suffering horribly, I am going to die, my God. I was so sad yesterday that I wanted to spend the evening somewhere other than at home, an evening that promised to be as long as the one before. The duke had come in the morning. It seems to me that the sight of this old man forgotten by death is making me die more quickly.

“Despite the burning fever that was consuming me, I had myself dressed and taken to the Vaudeville. Julie had put rouge on me, without which I would have looked like a corpse. I went to that box where I gave you our first rendezvous; the whole time, my eyes remained fixed on the orchestra seat you occupied that day and which yesterday was occupied by a sort of boor who laughed loudly at all the foolish things the actors were spouting. I was carried home half dead. I coughed and spat blood all night. Today I can no longer speak; I can scarcely move my arms. My God! My God! I am going to die. I expected it, but I cannot accustom myself to the idea of suffering more than I am suffering, and if...”
